title: Explain settlement patterns

blocks.heading: Explain settlement patterns
blocks.text: Climate, relief, economic opportunities, services and political conditions can influence settlement. Southern African settlement is uneven; water and suitable terrain can support concentration, while jobs and infrastructure may attract people even where physical conditions are difficult. One factor seldom explains the whole pattern.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Climate and relief
blocks.text: Water availability, temperature and terrain affect the feasibility of settlement and livelihoods. Gentler accessible land with usable water may support farming and building more readily than a dry steep area; infrastructure can modify some constraints.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Economic factors
blocks.text: Jobs, markets and transport can draw people towards productive opportunities. A viable workplace near a usable route can encourage settlement; a mineral deposit without access or work opportunities need not attract a large population.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Social factors
blocks.text: Schools, health facilities, family networks and other services can influence where people live. A service concentration may improve access, but housing and travel costs affect whether households can use it. Availability is different from equal access.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Political factors
blocks.text: Safety, displacement, boundaries and public settlement decisions can affect population distribution. Conflict can force movement regardless of a place’s productive potential; safer conditions and usable rights can support return. Do not assume movements are freely chosen.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the measure
blocks.text: Describe this fictional map specification: eight of ten settlements lie within 5 km of a river and all three market centres are on its road; the dry western area has two small settlements. Settlement is concentrated along the river-road corridor while the dry west is sparse. The settlement and market observations associate water and access with concentration without isolating either as the sole cause.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
